articleTitle: Anomaly-Based Intrusion Detection System for IoT Environment Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: IoT solutions have the potential to revolutionize our work and daily lives by providing the valuable data and insights. From enhancing the safety of roads, automobiles, and houses to fundamentally improving the way we produce and consume things. Regardless of the IoT system's advantages, some high-profile cyber attacks are preventing many firms from implementing IoT technologies. The current landscape of IoT ecosystem is characterized by complexity. Virtually any industry's equipment and objects can now be interconnected and configured to transmit data to cloud applications and back-end systems through cellular networks. Throughout the entire IoT journey, there is an inherent risk to digital security, with numerous hackers ready to exploit any vulnerabilities in the system. So, the need for security is very much important in IoT. In this paper, IoT system has been built to collect the dataset and perform intrusion to provide details of the data before and after the intrusion. Various machine learning models are used to classify tempered data.

articleTitle: Transform Domain Techniques combined with LBP for Tampered Image Detection using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: Detection of tampered images is very important for ensuring the authenticity of visual information in the domain of digital image forensics. In the context of machine learning, this research proposes methods for detecting tampered images using transform domain techniques such as discrete cosine transform (DCT), discrete wavelet transform (DWT). These techniques are combined with local binary pattern (LBP), which is effective at capturing local information. Dimensionality reduction is achieved with the help of principal component analysis (PCA) to reduce the number of features and analyzed the performance in terms of accuracy and time. Experiments have been conducted on CASIA 2.0 image tampering detection dataset which consists copy-move and splicing forgery images. Various classifiers, including Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), XG Boost, and Light GBM, are used to train machine learning models on the retrieved features. Based on the accuracy, precision, recall, fl-score, and execution time of these classifiers, the effectiveness of tamper detection is evaluated.

articleTitle: Fault Detection of Underwater Cables by Using Robotic Operating System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: This paper presents ROS, an open-source robot working framework. For correspondence among heterogeneous PC groups, ROS offers an organized correspondence layer on top of the host working framework, as opposed to an ordinary working framework that oversees booking and interaction the executives. This study describes how ROS may be used to securely and remotely control vehicles and other items without requiring human participation. The document also describes how ROS can be used to AUVs and how it fits into the present robot software architecture. The research also offers a method for inspecting optical cables that are buried or submerged utilizing a robotic operating system. In order to deploy this solution, ROS packages, including the ROS-Gazebo toolbox, are installed along with a virtual installation of Ubuntu OS using VMWare Workstation. Light radiation is being used as the main criterion to evaluate the state of the optical connection while the software is being evaluated using standard inputs.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Image Enhancement Techniques For Improving Blurry Identity Images
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: In digital image processing, enhancing the quality of Aadhar card images is paramount to ensure legibility and extract valuable information. This study investigates a comprehensive range of image enhancement techniques used to improve the quality and usability of Aadhar card images. The primary goal is to extract essential details and enhance the overall image's quality for future reference and digital preservation. The methods employed include Gaussian filtering for noise reduction, gamma correction for contrast enhancement, Unsharp Masking for edge enhancement, and contrast-limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) for improving overall image contrast and details of the blurry Aadhar images to evaluate the quality of resultant images two performance matrices are used Entropy and Standard deviation. The proposed approach is notably simpler and can potentially enhance the quality of archiving documents in digital images.

articleTitle: Intrusion Detection System for Live Anomaly-Based Network Packets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: In the evolving landscape of network technology, the surge in cyber-attacks poses a significant security risk, necessitating strong countermeasures. Many Intrusion detection systems have been proposed for countermeasures but there are not so many for anomaly-based detection. This article introduces a user interfaced Intrusion Detection System (IDS) which detect live individual packets in real-time for anomaly-based attacks, addressing the imperative of safeguarding computer networks and systems. The IDS classifies live individual or set of network packets in an in-depth manner and provides a pop up for the result. This system is designed to classify packets on a smaller but important set of attributes of network statistics. Due to comprehensive training and real-world adaptability, the IDS demonstrates precise classification of live packets originating from simulated attacks, thus offering a compelling advancement in intrusion detection capabilities.

articleTitle: Automatic Saline Monitoring System Using IoT
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: The need for health prevention is raising every day as the earth's population rises. Thus, everyone in our planet must take adequate care of their health. Due to technical breakthroughs in the domains medical treatment has improved fast in recent years, using sensors, microcontrollers, and computers to ensure quick patient recovery in hospitals. Every patient should receive better care, better monitoring, and the proper amount of essential nutrients at the proper time. By using an Internet of Things (IoT) to remotely monitor the saline system, the suggested method makes it possible to regulate saline drip rate using an improved technique. The suggested system includes a sensor for determining when the saline liquid level in the saline container has decreased to a risky level and a mechanism for stopping the saline flow automatically once the saline bottle is fully empty or at a specific level. The patients will benefit much from this, especially at night. Additionally, because air bubbles in blood may instantly kill a patient, this technique eliminates the deadly chance of their getting into their circulation. Such a gadget will guarantee that patients won't suffer any damage.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Algorithms for Cotton Plant Leaf Disease Classification from an Image
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: For disease diagnosis and yield optimization, the precise classification of pictures of cotton plant leaves into categories of healthy or diseased is a significant task in the agricultural sector. On a dataset of 2,310 photos that were made available to the public, we compared the performance of six categorization methods in this study. In terms of validation and test accuracy, our experimental results showed that ResNet50 performed better than other models, with ResNet50 reaching a validation accuracy of 0.980237 and a test accuracy of 0.9802. These results imply that ResNet is an excellent deep-learning model that can be used to accurately and dependably classify photos of cotton plant leaves in the agricultural sector. Our research demonstrates the capability of machine learning deep learning algorithms for disease diagnosis and yield improvement in the agriculture industry, which can ultimately lead to improved crop production and better food security.

articleTitle: A Technique for Maintaining Attribute-based Privacy Implementing Blockchain and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: Any wireless network is built on the mutually reinforcing pillars of privacy and security. Security measures often cover data connections, physical security, outside threats, and internal node operations. Whereas privacy covers the selective exchange of data among a network's various entities. To provide privacy to networks, many algorithms have been proposed by researchers in the past. Most of these algorithms utilize Graph-based anonymization approaches like l-diversity, k-anonymity, etc. These models do not scale well. Thus, this text proposes a machine learning-based block chain-powered privacy preservation protocol. The proposed protocol will perform attribute-based privacy with high efficiency due to the use of block chain architecture and will improve the overall Quality of Service of the network due to the integration of machine learning in the system.

articleTitle: The Utilization of Block-chain Innovation to Confirm KYC Records
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: Now this information is misused or disclosed, causing financial resources to explode and jeopardizing the entire online business. That's why education and online companies are keen to determine what to do with the roles of the Internet. We propose a solution that allows users to manage their own identities through block-chain self-management. This application allows users to secure their data on the block-chain by replacing servers. The use of block-chain allows users to securely record their personal data and information, ensuring the immutability and integrity of their information. Organizations play an important role in using methods to identify individuals for a variety of purposes, such as registration, loan approval, property management and access to schools. The solution is to create a block-chain infrastructure for users to store their content securely. It also provides a platform for users and organizations to participate in the block-chain network and store the information individuals need. Experts on the block-chain network verify personal identity. A block-chain server is used to make the block-chain lightweight. Additionally, a reward was introduced to encourage users/organizations on the block-chain network to share the identity information of all users. This approach not only ensures the security of personal information but also encourages participation in the verification process.

articleTitle: Enhancing Traffic Sign Detection and Classification through Multi-Task Learning Using CNNs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: Advanced driver assistance (ADA) systems are the technology behind self-driving cars. Still, other technologies play a crucial part in the advancing autonomous vehicles and driving assistance systems, one of them being Traffic Sign Recognition (TSR). The study aims to propose a neural network, specifically Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) based method for TSR using the Keras library. The model is trained, evaluated, and tested on the German Traffic Sign Recognition Benchmark (GTSRB) dataset. This image dataset has more than 50,000 labeled pictures of traffic signs representing 43 different classes. The proposed CNN model includes multiple convolutional layers, layers with maximum pooling, and fully connected layers for classification. The model is trained and tuned using the Adam optimizer and evaluated by calculating the accuracy is measured to evaluate the performance. The experiment results show that the suggested model is 98% accurate on the dataset. The proposed model can be used in TSR and various applications, specifically autonomous driving, assisting pedestrians, and traffic education. The suggested method effectively applies deep learning methods to recognize traffic signs and demonstrates their potential for use in the development of intelligent transportation systems.

articleTitle: Gender Classification Model based on the Resnet 152 Architecture
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: The objective of the gender categorization job is to determine a person's gender based on the face photographs of that individual. Approaches that are based on deep learning have shown encouraging outcomes in this field in recent years. A gender categorization model that is based on the Resnet 152 architecture is one of the contributions that this work makes. It has been shown that the Resnet 152 architecture can attain state-of-the-art performance on a variety of image recognition applications. This design is a deep residual neural network. We used a huge dataset of facial photos to fine-tune the previously trained Resnet 152 model, which can determine whether a person is a male or female based on the appearance of their face. The suggested model performed much better than numerous other state-of-the-art gender categorization models, with an accuracy of 99% on the test set. Our findings suggest that applying deep learning-based techniques for gender categorization is beneficial and that the Resnet 152 architecture has the potential to be used for this job.

articleTitle: Torsion Point Cryptography: Enhancing Data Security with Elliptic Curves
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: Torsion Point Cryptography is an innovative encryption technique that employs the mathematical properties of elliptic curves to ensure maximum security. This research paper delves into the technical intricacies of this approach, elucidating how it operates and why it is so effective. The authors delve into various types of torsion points that can be employed in this cryptography method, including rational and non-rational points, and discuss the benefits and constraints associated with each. They also conduct a thorough analysis of the security implications of torsion point cryptography, comparing it to other commonly used cryptosystems and highlighting its potential vulnerabilities. In conclusion, this paper offers an exhaustive introduction to torsion point cryptography and its real-world applications for secure communication.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Nature Inspired Optimization Algorithms for Biodiesel Yield Prediction using Extreme Learning Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: This study aims to enhance biodiesel yield prediction's precision by applying the advanced Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) model. The optimisation algorithms include Cuckoo Search, Dragonfly Optimization, Firefly Optimization, and Fruitfly Optimization to improve the predictive efficiency of the ELM model. Two datasets are investigated: biodiesel from Ceiba pentandra oil and the bio-oil yield using a Box-Behnken method for the experiment design. Optimisation approaches find the optimal hidden size of the ELM model. The results obtained from the first dataset reveal that Dragonfly Optimization was found to be the most effective algorithm, exhibiting the lowest Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.098 for Dataset I and 0.000306 for Dataset II and a strong relationship between predicted and actual values with a high coefficient of determination (R-squared) of 0.99 in both datasets. Firefly Optimization achieved exceptional accuracy for the second dataset with a hidden size of 28. High coefficient of determination values, low RMSE, and Mean Square Error (MSE) values highlight the predictive precision of Firefly Optimization. The comparative analysis underscores the potential of optimisation methods to significantly enhance biodiesel yield estimates, with Firefly Optimization and Dragonfly Optimization emerging as standout performers for their respective datasets. This study contributes valuable insights into biodiesel production by showcasing the efficiency of optimised ELM models in predicting biodiesel and bio-oil outputs.

articleTitle: Accounting for the Unaccounted Vulnerabilities Found in Endpoint ISP SOHO Router
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: This paper aims to explore and discuss the extent of configuration vulnerabilities found in the new generation of pre-configured SOHO routers provided by some of the top ISPs in the country, mainly India, and many in abroad as well. ISP-provided SOHO routers have become an integral part of our homes and offices today. With the previous generations of ADSL (Asymmetric Digital Subscriber Line) routers having shared their own set of vulnerabilities in the early 2000s, the world has since moved onto ADSL-based FTTH (Fiber To The Home) ONT (Optical Network Terminal) routers, which have not improved much over time in terms of security either. The authors will go through the exploits of these vulnerabilities performed in a controlled lab environment by using various types of attack vectors, such as directory enumeration attacks and compromising EOL software versions, along with assessing at the size of the impact they can bring about when performed in real-life scenarios. Finally, this paper will discuss some stringent measures that ISPs can take to better implement their router security and harden their firmware to mitigate these attacks on their networks. This paper primarily focuses on the security measures that ISPs can implement to prevent attacks on their networks, and less on the measures that individual users of these ISP can take to protect their devices from getting compromised.

articleTitle: Alignment Free Fingerprint Template Security Using Minutia Neighbors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: Creating a secured fingerprint biometric template is a challenging task. Advances in the field of fingerprint reconstruction from minutia features make the task of fingerprint template security to be essential. In this article, a fingerprint security template is proposed using k nearest neighborhood pattern starting from the minutia features. Also, a template matching method is proposed based on threshold score. The proposed template security method does not involve template alignment in the matching stage. The proposed method is evaluated using the FVC 2002 protocol based recognition on a benchmarked dataset.

articleTitle: Real Time Automated Sign Language Recognition and Transcription with Audio Feedback
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: Sign language recognition and transcription systems that operate automatically can greatly enhance communication for those people who are deaf. These innovative techniques hold the promise of breaking down barriers and fostering greater inclusivity for individuals with hearing impairments. An automated real-time system is developed that recognizes American Sign Language (ASL) gestures and responds to the user with corresponding text output along with audio feedback. The proposed system works by capturing the hand gestures, extract the features or data points using Suzuki contour algorithm and implements Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) algorithm to classify American Sign Language gestures in real-time. This system uses lemmatization algorithm for transcribing the gestures into text and converts the text to audio feedback using text-to-speech synthesis module. The proposed system is based on computer vision and deep learning techniques for sign recognition, natural language processing for transcription, and text-to-speech synthesis for audio feedback. The proposed system performance is accessed using a MNIST dataset of ASL gestures taken from Kaggle, and its effectiveness has been demonstrated in real-world scenarios. The system achieves a high accuracy of 91% in sign recognition and transcription and produces high-quality audio feedback in real-time. The proposed system has the potential to improve communication and accessibility and for deaf and hard-of-hearina individuals in various contexts.

articleTitle: Understanding Twitter Emojis for Sentiment Analysis and Risk Perception on Royal Palace of Naples, Italy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: In the realm of safety and security management, assessing the perceived risk among visitors to heritage and cultural sites holds significant importance. Social media emerges as a potent tool in this context, as it propagates reviews that can sway individual opinions. It stands as a pivotal medium for advertising, with a staggering 90% of tourists relying on these reviews. Recent times have witnessed a surge in research concerning opinion mining and sentiment analysis, driven by the imperative of enhancing public safety and security. Such investigations empower security personnel to uncover unforeseen incidents that may pose threats. In certain instances, perceived risks may be magnified. Consequently, it becomes imperative to identify the underlying reasons for such apprehension and implement corresponding mitigation measures. In this paper, we delve into the estimation of risk perception at the Royal Palace of Naples in Italy. We demonstrate how this estimation can elicit emotional responses from visitors through the application of sentiment analysis on Twitter data, including the analysis of emojis.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Malware Detection: Feature-Based Approach for Targeting Diverse Malware Categories
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: In today's digital landscape, the task of identifying various types of malicious files has become progressively challenging. Modern malware exhibits increasing sophistication, often evading conventional anti-malware solutions. The scarcity of data on distinct and novel malware strains further complicates effective detection. In response, this research presents an innovative approach to malware detection, specifically targeting multiple distinct categories of malicious software. In the initial stage, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is performed and achieved a remarkable accuracy rate of 95.39%. Our methodology revolves around leveraging features commonly accessible from user-uploaded files, aligning with the contextual behavior of typical users seeking to identify malignancy. This underscores the efficacy of the unique feature-based detection strategy and its potential to enhance contemporary malware identification methodologies. The outcomes achieved attest to the significance of addressing emerging malware threats through inventive analytical paradigms.

articleTitle: Physical Biometric Spoofing of 3D Dynamic On-Air Signature
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: 3D on-air signatures represent a novel behavioral biometric that is highly challenging to imitate, even from a distance. However, the emergence of robotic arms capable of mimicking human movements poses a potential security vulnerability. This paper examines the possibility of generating 3D fingertip movements with a robotic arm that accurately mimic a 3D on-air signature to circumvent a biometric system. The robotic arm controls trajectory and velocity to generate a human-like movement. Robotic-made signatures are then used to spoof a 3D on-air dynamic signature biometric system, which relies on a DTW verifier. Experiments demonstrate that robotic signatures can effectively bypass a verifier exclusively trained with real signatures, underscoring the importance of incorporating an additional security layer, such as a liveness detector, into these biometric schemes.

articleTitle: A Protection Approach For Coal Miners Safety Helmet Using IoT
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: The goal of the coal mining helmet proposed in this research is to provide insurance to miners by forewarning them. As long as the person is carrying the protective cap, all of the components may be mentioned. The output of the cap module is updated continually for each example, updating the cloud with real-time data. These wearable devices can share their data or retrieve it from other sources thanks to the Internet of Things (IOT). If there is a threat, warnings are given to the employer and the digger. The creation of wearable PC frameworks and universal registration has tremendously aided the advancement of wearable technology. As a result, this wearable device includes a wide range of sensors that allow it to connect with other parts and enhance the insurance of the digger. The equipment has integrated data gathering, information management, and information correspondence parts. The DHT11 temperature and humidity sensor was employed. There are times when the heat and moisture levels in mines are too high and the excavator dies. Anyone inside the mines should have respiratory problems as a result of those gases being released, which could lead to suffocation. A caution is sent to both the base Authorizer and the digger in the far-fetched occasion that at least one of these pieces go past the breaking point.

articleTitle: Jal-Tarang: Smart Buoy for Wave Height Measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: Smart buoys have emerged as a promising technology for accurate and real-time wave height measurement in coastal regions and maritime environments. These buoys utilize advanced sensors and communication systems to collect and transmit data on wave heights, enabling improved safety, planning, and decision-making. This paper provides an overview of the concept of smart buoys for wave height measurement, discussing the technological advancements, data accuracy, and potential applications. It also highlights the integration of smart buoys into data networks and the future developments in this field. The findings emphasize the significance of smart buoys in enhancing our understanding of wave behavior and their impact on various sectors and industries

articleTitle: Threat Modeling of Cube Orange Based Unmanned Aerial Vehicle System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are being utilised more often across a variety of sectors, hence their security must be prioritised. To detect threats, weak points, and effective defences against malicious assaults, UAV threat modeling is essential. The significance of methodically evaluating risks, comprehending weaknesses, and putting security measures in place is emphasised in this study. The process of threat modeling is touched upon, including the system's scoping, information collecting, threat and vulnerability identification, risk assessment, and countermeasure implementation. In the domain of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), the paper recommends using a modified version of the Microsoft Threat Modeling Tool to undertake threat modeling. A methodical methodology to identify, assess, and prioritize possible risks and vulnerabilities particular to UAV systems is provided by the Microsoft Threat Modeling Tool. Stakeholders, such as UAV operators, manufacturers, and security experts, may use threat modeling methods to undertake a comprehensive assessment of the security state of their UAV systems. Users may proactively address security issues and improve the resilience of UAV systems in the face of emerging threats by undertaking efficient threat modeling.

articleTitle: Biometric Authentication from sEMG: Assessing the Potential of Adaptive Chirp Mode Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: Surface electromyography (sEMG)-based biometrics authentication has drawn a significant attention in recent years as a promising methodology. This technique takes advantage of the distinctive electrical activity patterns that muscles produce when performing various gestures. Individual differences can be observed during training for multiple users which led the researchers towards biometric investigations using sEMG. This paper proposes the biometric authentication using sEMG signals based on adaptive chirp mode decomposition (ACMD). The recorded sEMG signals are decomposed into its modes using ACMD and further each mode is segmented using windowing approach. The time domain (TD) and auto regressive (AR) model based features are extracted from each segment. The authentication performance is investigated for normal test scenario. Results show the performance of the selected 4-channel configuration with average equal error rate (EER) of 2.402%. The comparative authentication performance claims that proposed method authenticate with better values of performance parameters than the existing method.

articleTitle: Classification of Malware Using Deep Learning: A Study
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: Malware, or malicious software, significantly threatens data privacy and system security. This study delves into image-based malware classification, employing deep learning techniques. This research addresses the early stages of the classification of malware using image-based deep learning approaches. Our study emphasizes the exploration of diverse methodologies to enhance malware classification efficiency. We acknowledge image-based classification, with substantial potential for improved accuracy and robustness in malware classification. Additionally, we conduct a comprehensive comparative analysis, contrasting our image-based approach with existing methods. Through rigorous experimentation, we achieve 97.3% accuracy rate, highlighting the effectiveness of our approach. In conclusion, the study aims to contribute to evolving cybersecurity practices by exploring this domain for more precise and efficient malware classification.

articleTitle: KILLS-1: An Analysis on the Present Security Trends and Proposal of a Multilingual Encryption Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: Cryptography is the art of hiding information and protecting the originality and the confidentiality of the information. With an increase in technology and generation of huge amounts of data in trillions of storage, it becomes crucial to deploy security algorithms in order to ensure the integrity of the data. In the present date there are many scenarios where different cryptographic algorithms are being implemented. However, it is equally important to measure their robustness towards different attacks which are taking place with malicious intentions. Currently most of the systems and the data present are being secured in a monolingual pattern where with the advancements of the recent technology it has become easier to intercept these systems.Multilingualism while on the other hand acts as a bridge in connecting diverse societies. The combination of Multilingualism and Cryptography leading to Multilingual Cryptography is an approach which focuses on implementing an additional layer of security to the already existing systems. It can also be defined as a technological advancement which transcends language barriers and fortifies secure global communication. Through this paper different existing cryptographic algorithms in different scenarios and an approach on how multilingualism cryptography can be implemented are discussed. The algorithm of Key in Indian Linguistic Languages Security also abbreviated as KILLS-1 is also proposed through this paper and the concept and its working has been explained as well which aims at increasing the robustness and safety of the existing security systems.

articleTitle: Multi-Class Network Intrusion Detection Using Deep Neural Networks Tuned on Imbalanced Data
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: As computer networks become ubiquitous, they face escalating risks from cyberattacks that can severely disrupt critical infrastructure. Existing network intrusion detection datasets have limitations like inadequate diversity of samples and poor classification accuracy. This research utilizes the University of Nevada - Reno Intrusion Detection Dataset (UNR-IDD) encompassing normal traffic and 5 different intrusion types to develop a deep neural network for multi-class intrusion detection. After exploratory data analysis, a baseline Multi-Layer Perceptron model was developed. A structured tuning methodology involving ANOVA feature selection and grid search hyperparameter optimization is followed to improve validation performance. The research quantitatively demonstrates the impact of methodical tuning guided by validation accuracy, establishing a template for developing high-performance deep learning intrusion detection systems. With further enhancements, the techniques explored could equip security experts with invaluable intelligence to protect networks against sophisticated cyber threats

articleTitle: Insight Now: A Cross-Platform News Application for Real-Time and Personalized News Aggregation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: In an era characterized by rapid technological advancements, the ability to communicate instantly with others has become an integral part of our daily lives. With the ubiquity of mobile devices, tablets, and laptops, staying informed about the latest events and news has never been easier. This research article explores the development and impact of an Android news application that connects users to the latest news from over 120 reputable news organizations across India. The primary objective of this innovative application is to amalgamate global news sources and present information to users in an engaging and visually compelling format with minimal delay. One of the distinguishing features of this Android news app is its user-centric approach, allowing individuals to filter live news based on their preferences. Upon selecting a news article, users are seamlessly redirected to the corresponding news source, ensuring the integrity of the original reporting. The app is designed to deliver frequent updates on a wide range of topics, leveraging the capabilities of the NEWS API to source information from renowned news outlets worldwide, including BBC, CNN, The Guardian, and NDTV. This research anticipates a substantial increase in the speed at which information reaches the average person, thanks to the seamless integration of multiple news sources through this Android news application. This technological advancement promises to revolutionize the way individual's access and consume news, ensuring they stay well-informed in an increasingly fast-paced world.

articleTitle: Detecting Diabetic Retinopathy using ResNet50 and Explainable AI
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy, a common complication of diabetes, can lead to vision impairment and blindness if not detected early. Current diagnostic methods, involving manual examination of fundus images, can be time-consuming. This paper proposes an innovative approach that combines deep learning models with Explainable AI techniques, such as the SHAP method, to enhance the interpretability of diabetic retinopathy detection. This combination allows for more accurate identification of the disease stage and provides insights into the model's decision-making process, which can guide treatment and interventions. The proposed approach aims to improve the accuracy, fairness, transparency, and outcomes of diabetic retinopathy detection, fostering trust in AI models and enabling informed decision-making in healthcare settings.

articleTitle: Locating People in a Confined Space Using iBeacon Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: Current location or monitoring systems are a set of several technologies that allow you to monitor the movement of different people or objects in both indoor and outdoor areas. These include Global Position System, Radio-frequency identification, Near-Field Communication, Bluetooth Low Energy beacon, Video Surveillance Systems, Intruder and Hold-up Alarm Systems, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, QR codes, etc. All these technologies have their technical limits. Not every system is usable both in normal operating mode (e.g. attendance monitoring, logistics processes) and in mode triggered by an emergency or situation (e.g. due to the spread of an infectious disease such as COVID-19). A long-term research activity of the authors of the article is the development of a technical solution that would allow monitoring and tracing of persons or objects (entities), not only outdoors but also closed environments (e.g. with low level of GPS signal). This solution would also be usable in both normal and specific modes. One of the possible technical solutions is the iBeacon technology, which works on the principle of Bluetooth Low Energy and which, in addition to commercial applications, can also be used in the field of security and safety. The article focuses on determining the position of an entity in inner space using iBeacon technology, using various approaches, such as determining position by assigning distance to a specific level of RSSI signal, determining position based on the ratio of RSSI signal level of opposite sensors, or determining position based on the “fingerprinting” method.

articleTitle: SL-Defender: Decentralized Defense for Adversarial Robustness in Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: Adversarial poisoning attacks are growing threats to federated deep learning systems, as models can be poisoned from any of the compromised participants. Existing solutions attempt to detect and defend these attacks by assuming that there is an honest central parameter aggregator on which the detection and defense techniques can be applied. This assumption can give rise to a single point of failure (SPOF) and an easy target for attackers to compromise the whole federated learning system. They also lack a robust mechanism to isolate the malicious node so as to protect the rest of the federated system. We propose SL-Defender, a novel solution that overcomes these limitations by using a decentralized method to detect and defend against attacks based on Swarm Learning. Our solution uses the selected layers from each of the federated learning participants and projects their parameters into a lower dimensional subspace and performs clustering analysis in this subspace. The proposed methodology adds the ability to act on identified malicious participants and contain their impact on the federated learning process or remove them if needed. The proposed SL-Defender thus eliminates the need for honest central aggregator and distributes computation to peers and dynamically monitors them and defends them from the federating poisoned parameters without interrupting the learning process. With the support of experimental results on MNIST Dataset, we prove that SL-Defender will offer a unique position to improve the reliability and trustworthiness of Swarm Learning and Federated Machine learning in general.

articleTitle: Fed-Trace: An Efficient Model to Traceback Data Poisoning Attacks in Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: Privacy-preserving federated learning has been a widely adopted technology due to its ability to protect sensitive data while enabling collaborative model training across multiple organizations or devices. But despite all its advantages, it is also prone to insider attacks due to its lack of access to the client's data. To traceback such attacks and identify clients with malicious intent, an innovative traceback methodology has been proposed in this work, which is designed to traceback data poisoning attacks in federated learning systems. While various defense mechanisms have been proposed for countering such attacks, the aspect of forensics is not much explored. The proposed approach leverages the unique characteristics of federated learning, where data accessibility is limited, and it utilizes gradients recommended by each clients instead of their training data for identifying malicious clients. The proposed work uses a recursive clustering and pruning algorithm on these gradients to identify and remove benign clients until it is left with only malicious clients. Through various experiments, the proposed work demonstrates its ability to trace malicious clients. These experiments have been done on the CIFAR10 dataset and employed Unlearnable CIFAR10 as clean label poisoning data. By combining principles of federated learning, recursion, clustering, poisoning attacks, and forensics, the proposed methodology aims to enhance the detection and understanding of poisoning attacks in federated learning environments, contributing to the overall security and integrity of these systems against various kinds of poisoning attacks.

articleTitle: Intelligent IOT-based BMS for Integrated Solar with AC grid Fast Charging Systems in Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: Environmental pollution is the biggest concern these days' electric cars are introduced as a less polluting solution, especially for fossil fuels which are reduced considerably and there is no release of any harmful gas. Due to the long charging time of the battery, electric vehicles often face problems. This research paper aims to offer a portable charger coupled converter (AC-DC) with a solar charge controlled (DC-DC) converter used to charge lithium-ion battery packs used in EV technology. Intelligence added for the maintenance of safety standards through IoT-based BMS controlling, which helps for wide range data storage over the cloud and helps in data analysis & monitoring the important safety parameters of the battery along with accurate SoC (State of charge) & SoH (State of Health) estimation of any type of Li-ion battery chemistry cells. Most EV batteries catch fire it's hard to predict the reasons as all data will be lost with BMS hardware damage with temperature but it can be avoided by IOT-based data collection applicable to any type of battery used in EV. At the time when charging is full, the system automatically disconnects the charger from the battery. When this system is used, the time taken for charging is reduced and other parameters are monitored as well, and this is done under a highly specialized system of intelligence and related settings. It is important to note that the system of battery management has no impact on thermal performance.

articleTitle: Enhancing Sentiment Analysis Accuracy in IMDb Movie Reviews with Deep Learning Models: A Comparative Study of RNN and CNN Models
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: Sentiment analysis, a key problem in NLP, has enormous relevance in interpreting human emotions and viewpoints from textual data. With a strong emphasis on the transformative function of hyperparameter tuning, we set out on an exhaustive exploration of deep learning models designed for sentiment analysis in this study. Our study covers a range of model designs, from the basic LSTM Model to the complex LSTM + CNN Model with Hyperparameter Tuning. We demonstrate the critical role of hyperparameter optimization on model performance, particularly in improving prediction accuracy, by rigorous experimentation. Among the models examined, the perfectly tuned LSTM and CNN Model stands out as the model with the highest level of accuracy, highlighting the importance of hyperparameter tuning. Readers can gain a thorough grasp of model performances through a thorough accuracy table and a visually appealing Bar Chart for accuracy comparison. As textual data continues to proliferate in the world of digital media, our research shines as a beacon of empirical successes, illuminating the crucial role that hyperparameter tweaking plays in obtaining superior sentiment analysis outcomes. These results not only advance the science of sentiment analysis but also provide insightful information for practical uses where comprehending human emotion is crucial.

articleTitle: Detection and Mitigation Mechanisms for Covert Channel Attack
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: Numerous individuals have long been fascinated by covert communication across a network of connections. It has enticed not only trustworthy entities to communicate covertly with one another, but also attackers/hackers to develop techniques to discover and disclose information and to exploit the system in ways that violate security protocols. Employing covert channels to transport data in a secure manner. Encryption merely prevents unauthorised entities from decrypting interaction, whereas covert channels seek to conceal the interaction's actual presence. These channels were first identified as a security risk on monolithic structures, such as mainframe computer systems. In recent years, computer network protocols have shifted their focus to covert channel routes. The Internet's vast quantity of information and diversity of diverse protocols make it an ideal high-bandwidth medium for private communications. This survey provides an overview of the mechanisms employed for the detection and mitigation of covert channel-specific attacks that may compromise the confidentiality of the data being transmitted between two sources. Finally, the concluding remarks along with the future possibilities of the covert channel attacks are indicated.

articleTitle: The New Communication Network for an Internet of Things/Everything Based Security/Safety/General Management/Visitor's Services Integrated System of the Pompeii Archeological Park, Italy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: Pompeii is renowned for its disastrous chronicle, as in 79 A.D. an awful explosion of Vesuvius volcano totally interred it with all its population. Just in 1748 A.D., by the choice of the Bourbons monarchs, explorations started in Pompeii and thus the beginning of the diggings. Starting from that period, the notoriety of Pompeii diffused through the globe due to its treasures and, although several valuable objects have been looted and stripped during the centuries, it still continues to astonish nowadays. With its different millions tourists per year, the Pompeii Archaeological Park, only after the Colosseum in Rome, is the most visited place in Italy. An exclusive and composite cultural heritage site, as the considered one, requires considerable efforts to warrant people security and safety. Further, it is vital to warrant cultural heritage preservation and protection as well as accessibility for people, with particular reference to people with disabilities, and for personnel normally working for site managing. These goals can be achieved employing integrated systems and innovative technologies, such as Internet of Things / Everything (IoT/IoE) that can connect people, things (mobile terminals, intelligent sensors, devices, wearable devices; etc.), data/information/knowledge and particular processes. The goal of this paper is to illustrate the IoT/IoE integrated system and the method and the outcomes attained from the study and the project of a new communication network for Internet of Things/Everything based security/safety/general management and visitors' services integrated system of the Pompeii archaeological park, Italy.

articleTitle: Pseudo Random Binary Sequence using Lattice-based Hard Problem for Quantum Key Distribution
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: Recently, there has been a growing interest among researchers in Pseudo-Random Binary Sequences (PRBS) for Quantum Key Distribution (QKD). QKD is a cryptographic protocol that distributes secret keys between senders and receivers, relying on random numbers to determine the basis for evaluating transmitted bits. Quantum Random Number Generators (QRNG) utilizing natural resources create random bit sequences for QKD. However, QRNGs are susceptible to natural noise, which compromises their security. Additionally, post-processing of QRNG-generated sequences is necessary to reduce noise, but this process slows down the random number generation speed in QKD. Non-deterministic Pseudo-Random Sequence Generators (ND-PRSG) may overcome the QRNG's constraints, post-processing, and speed. Lattice-based NDPRSG provides security and efficiency. The proposed work focuses on generating a uniform PRBS with non-deterministic entropy using Learning with Errors (LWE) and LFSR. NIST Statistical Tests are performed on generated PRBS for randomness analysis, and the results are reported. The proposed PRBS generation can be used for QKD, operating up to 20.17 Mbit/s.

articleTitle: A Study on Privacy-Preserving Auctions Considering Possible Collusions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: An auction can be used in various domains, such as cloud computing, data trading, energy trading, and spectrum allocation, which can help to identify the true value of selling goods. The introduction of the Internet has already paved the way for electronic auction (e-auction). Electronic auctions have several benefits over traditional physical auctions; however, in e-auctions, privacy becomes a major issue. Many works are reported in the literature to address this issue. Collusion of various entities involved in the auction, such as bidder, seller, auctioneer, etc. However, most works related to privacy-preserving auctions lack the consideration of collusion of involved entities. In this paper, we have discussed various important works related to privacy-preserving auctions and their associated issues. Problems created due to the collusion of entities in the works are also discussed. We also summarized works in allied disciplines where privacy-preserving auctions are applied. We have also discussed the future research directions in brief.

articleTitle: Enhancing Online Job Posting Security: A Big Data Approach to Fraud Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: In the digital era, online employment platforms have revolutionized the hiring landscape, offering unprecedented convenience and accessibility to both employers and job seekers. Nevertheless, this newfound ease has attracted malicious entities seeking to exploit the system through the dissemination of deceptive job listings. These fraudulent activities pose significant threats to businesses and individuals, encompassing financial losses, damage to reputation, and potential legal ramifications. This study leverages Apache Spark and Big Data to develop an advanced fraud detection system for online job postings. Our primary objective is to enhance the precision and efficiency of detecting and preventing fraudulent job advertisements. This will be achieved through the comprehensive analysis and processing of vast datasets extracted from various employment websites. By harnessing the power of these cutting-edge technologies, our investigation aims to fortify the integrity of online employment platforms, safeguarding the interests of both employers and job seekers alike.

articleTitle: A Recent Study of Security Techniques for IoT
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: IoT signifies “Internet of Things.”. It is upgraded version of Embedded system. It is mainly used for connecting things, exchange real time data in order to improve digital intelligence to devices that boast productivity, efficiency, services, and many more. IoT Connections are between the human and sensors or sensors to sensors. From the billions of devices that are interconnected, the internet creates an intelligence system. The IoT exchanges data in the cloud or in a warehouse. It analyses and predicts information that will significantly change business and our lives. More connected devices translate to more areas for attack and openings for hackers. If we ignore these security issues, the situation will become worse, and devastation may occur. There are many types of existing security techniques that prove high security, but they are not specific to the IoT. In this work, we will concentrate on current lightweight cryptographic security solutions that are being utilised or proposed for safe data transfer in the IoT sector.

articleTitle: A Survey of Disease Detection in Cauliflower Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: Agriculture holds a vital role in India's economy, with a significant portion of its population reliant on this sector. The success of agricultural production is influenced by environmental factors beyond human control, such as weather conditions. Disease, however, is a controllable parameter that can impact crop productivity and quality. Proper disease management is essential to enhance crop output and reduce the need for harmful pesticides. Among the essential crops, cauliflower has gained prominence in India due to its nutritional value and economic benefits. However, the application of pesticides on cauliflower poses health risks, emphasizing the need for early disease detection. For many years, scientists have researched how to deal with the common diseases of Cauliflower is susceptible to various diseases, with researchers primarily focusing on white rust, black rot, bacterial soft rot and downy mildew. However, there are still many diseases and parts of Cauliflower have not been completed. This paper conducts a comprehensive survey and analysis of disease classification and detection techniques specifically applied to identify cauliflower diseases. The paper evaluates the strengths and limitations of the proposed methodologies. We talk about how diseases in plants are automatically detected by using machine learning and deep learning. Our investigation places a particular emphasis on the recent developments in deep learning methodologies over the past five years. Additionally, we provide an in-depth analysis of various datasets pertaining to plant diseases. Our objective is to clarify the details about the diseases and how to detect them promptly with machine learning, deep learning and CNN technologies.

articleTitle: Statistical and Deep Learning Approach for Kannada Parts of Speech Tagger
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: With over 64 million native speakers, Kannada is one of the major languages of the Dravidian Language family in India. However, it confronts considerable difficulties when it comes to linguistic resources for processing and computing. Basic NLP operations like lemmatization, parts of speech tagging, machine-translation, sentiment analysis and recognizing named entities tasks are greatly hindered by its complex morphology and agglutinative nature. In our research work, we aim to obtain the best results in parts of speech tagging for Kannada. We achieve this by working on both CRF and Bi-LSTM, along with two widely used word embedding techniques: Word2Vec(implemented using Gensim) and IndicNLP. By meticulously applying these methodologies to two distinct datasets, we have produced a total of six distinctive models. Our research deeply explores the contrast and comparison of these models, leading us to identify the most proficient model among them. This exhaustive analysis culminates in the discovery that the Bi-LSTM model attains an impressive F1-score of 0.921 and test accuracy of 86.2%. These outcomes are primarily drawn from the primary dataset sourced from Siva Reddy, a renowned author in this field.

articleTitle: 3D Synthetic On-Air Signatures for Biometric Attack
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: The importance of authentication is paramount when it comes to the protection of resources, encompassing both physical corporate facilities and digital assets. Among the different authentication methodologies, 3D on-air signatures represent a novel behavioral biometric that is highly challenging to imitate, even when observed from a distance. However, the emergence of robotic arms capable of mimicking human movements poses a potential security vulnerability for these emerging schemes. This paper focuses on examining the possibility of generating 3D fingertip movements that accurately mimic a signature, with the intention of circumventing a biometric system. We utilize the iDeLog3D algorithm to produce artificial movements of the fingertips, based on the 3D Sigma-Lognormal model and the Kinematic Theory of Rapid Movements. We then replicate a 3D on-air database using this model and proceed to compare the performance of a DTW-based signature verifier using both real and synthetic signatures. During the experiments, it has been demonstrated that synthetic signatures are effective in bypassing a signature verifier that is exclusively trained using real signatures. This underscores the importance of incorporating an additional layer of security, such as a bot detector, into these types of biometric schemes.

articleTitle: Tourist Place Classification Using Topic Modeling Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST)
abstract: Today social media is one of the most powerful and popular tool which is expanding rapidly in the world. Many tourism websites publish tourist places data for describing places in the form of Description. Over this data, Analysis can be performed and meaningful insights can be drawn. By analyzing this data we can find the subject or topic discussed in Description. By performing topic modeling over these data we can predict the category of tourist place. Also topic Modeling can help to cluster textual content into groups as per the subject of the text. In research study, Comparative analysis of topic modeling algorithms has been performed which will find a category of tourist places. Tourist place description blog data was gathered from tourism websites. Using tourist place Description dataset, comparative study of Topic modeling algorithms i.e. LDA Variational Inference(VI) algorithm and LDA Gibbs Sampling(GS) algorithm has been performed. Results of experiments has been analyzed with performance evaluation using various factors such as coherence score, perplexity, training execution time and accuracy percentage. LDA Gibbs Sampling(GS) algorithm outperforms LDA Variational Inference (VI) algorithm in terms of coherence score, perplexity, accuracy percentage. Whereas, LDA Variational Inference(VI) algorithm requires less execution time as compared to the LDA Gibbs Sampling(GS) algorithm
